chunks: 3388 - Hammad ibn Isa narrated from someone who informed him, from Hariz, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
The first upon whom lots were cast was Maryam bint 'Imran, and this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
And you were not with them when they cast their pens as to which of them should take charge of Maryam.

And the lots were six. Then they cast lots concerning Yunus عليه السلام when he embarked with the people, and the ship was caught in the deep waters. So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Yunus three times. He said: Then Yunus عليه السلام went to the front of the ship, and there was the whale with its mouth open, so he cast himself in.

Then 'Abd al-Muttalib had nine sons, so he vowed regarding the tenth that if Allah granted him a boy, he would sacrifice him. When 'Abd Allah was born, he was not able to sacrifice him, while the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was in his loins. So he brought ten camels and cast lots between them and 'Abd Allah, and the lots came out against 'Abd Allah. Then he added ten more. The lots continued to come out against 'Abd Allah, and he kept adding ten, until when they reached one hundred, the lots came out against the camels. Then 'Abd al-Muttalib said, 'I have not done justice to my Lord,' so he repeated the lots three times, and they came out against the camels. He said, 'Now I know that my Lord is pleased,' so he slaughtered them.

key_terms.أَقْلَامَهُمْ: their pens, used in the Qur'anic account for casting lots over the care of Maryam
key_terms.السِّهَامُ: the lots or shares used for drawing lots
key_terms.الْإِبِلِ: the camels offered in place of 'Abd Allah after the lots fell upon them
key_terms.الْحُوتُ: the whale that swallowed Yunus عليه السلام
key_terms.عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: 'Abd Allah, father of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, for whom lots were cast against camels
key_terms.عَبْدُ الْمُطَّلِبِ: 'Abd al-Muttalib, grandfather of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, whose vow is described
key_terms.مَرْيَمُ: Maryam, daughter of 'Imran, mentioned here as the first person concerning whom lots were cast
key_terms.يُونُسَ: Prophet Yunus عليه السلام, upon whom the lot fell during the ship incident

ai.seo_question: What examples of drawing lots are mentioned in the Qur'an and early sacred history?
ai.summary: This hadith cites the Qur'anic account of Maryam عليها السلام as an example of drawing lots and then mentions the case of Yunus عليه السلام and the vow of 'Abd al-Muttalib. It shows the use of lots in earlier sacred history and connects the practice to Qur'anic narrative and transmitted tradition.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3388 - Narrated by Hammad ibn Isa, from someone who informed him, from Hariz, from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as):
"The first person upon whom casting lots (Qur'ah) was performed was Maryam (Mary), the daughter of Imran. This is based on the saying of Allah (swt), the Exalted:
'And you were not with them when they cast their pens as to which of them should be responsible for Maryam.' (Surah Aal-E-Imran 3:44).

The lots were six in number. Then they cast lots for Yunus (as) (Jonah (as)) when he sailed with a group of people. When the ship was caught in turbulence, they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Yunus three times." Imam (as) continued: "Yunus (as) proceeded to the edge of the ship, and there was the whale with its mouth wide open. So he threw himself in.

Similarly, when Abdul Muttalib (as) had nine sons, he vowed that if Allah (swt) granted him a tenth son, he would sacrifice him. When Abdullah (as) was born, he could not bear to sacrifice him, as the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was in his lineage. So Abdul Muttalib (as) brought ten camels and cast lots between them and Abdullah (as). The lot fell on Abdullah (as). He added ten more camels and repeated the process. The lot continued to fall on Abdullah (as), and he kept increasing the camels by ten each time. Finally, when the number of camels reached one hundred, the lot fell on the camels. Abdul Muttalib (as) then said: 'I have not yet done justice to my Lord (azj),' and repeated the lot three more times. When it fell on the camels each time, he said: 'Now I know my Lord (azj) is satisfied.' So he sacrificed the camels."
